title: Monorail Hoist
model_title: Monorail Electric Chain Hoist (Curved I-Beam Track)

introduction.definition: A monorail hoist runs on a single fixed I-beam track, which may be straight or curved. A trolley rolls on the lower flange of the beam and carries an electric chain or wire-rope hoist. It moves loads along a fixed path — for example from a loading bay to a machine or around a production line.
applications: Moving loads along a fixed route (curves, switches)
key_points: Trolley runs on the lower flange
Curves and switches allow complex routes
introduction.summary: A monorail hoist runs on a single I-beam track, which can curve to follow a process route. The trolley carries an electric chain or wire-rope hoist that lifts the load; it moves goods between fixed points such as machines or loading bays.

script.narration: This module introduces the Monorail Hoist.
A monorail hoist runs on a single fixed I-beam track, which may be straight or curved.
A trolley rolls on the lower flange of the beam and carries an electric chain or wire-rope hoist.
It moves loads along a fixed path — for example from a loading bay to a machine or around a production line.
Typical applications include production and assembly lines; moving loads along a fixed route (curves, switches); maintenance lifting over equipment rows; warehouses.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Monorail Hoist — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Monorail Hoist.
Pre-use check of hoist, chain, hook latch and limit switches.
Measure chain wear and lubricate; check track wear and hangers.
Thorough examination; overhaul hoist.
Watch for wire rope damage: broken wires, kinks, corrosion. Common cause: wear on sheaves/drum, overload, poor spooling.
Watch for brake failure: load drift, increased stopping distance. Common cause: worn linings, contamination, wrong adjustment.
Watch for overload: trip of limiter, structural deformation. Common cause: unknown load weight, side pulling.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
